title: The Kingdom Where the Sovereign's End Went Unseen
intro: History has known rulers of every kind, but few commanded a domain quite like this one. Where the wind itself answered to their command and laborers no mortal eye could see toiled in silence, this reign was unlike any before or after. Yet even the grandest of kingdoms must end—and when this one did, the truth emerged from a source so humble that no one had thought to suspect it.
clues: I was granted a vast kingdom by my Lord, spoken of across the sacred pages.
I inherited great wisdom and authority from a parent who walked before me in devotion.
I commanded the very wind, and it traveled far for my purposes.
Beings unseen to ordinary eyes labored under my authority, constructing wonders beyond compare.
Springs of molten copper flowed for me, a blessing unique among those chosen by Allah.
When I departed from this world, my body remained standing against a staff. Only when a small creature of the earth ate through that staff did those around me realize I had passed.

arabic: فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَوْتَ مَا دَلَّهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَوْتِهِۦٓ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلْأَرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُۥ ۖ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلْجِنُّ أَن لَّوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْغَيْبَ مَا لَبِثُوا۟ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ
verse: And when We decreed for him [i.e., Solomon] death, nothing indicated to them [i.e., the jinn] his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff. But when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment. (34:14)
